query: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange RFC 8693 workload identity
title: RFC 8693 OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange January 2020
snippet: RFC 8693 defines a protocol for an HTTP- and JSON-based Security Token Service (STS) by defining how to request and obtain security tokens from OAuth 2.0 authorization servers, including security tokens employing impersonation and delegation.
claim: RFC 8693 defines HTTP/JSON-based token exchange for obtaining security tokens with impersonation and delegation support.

query: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange RFC 8693 workload identity
title: Token Exchange — OAuth 2.0
snippet: A new grant type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange is defined in the specification. The Token Exchange grant can be used to exchange tokens to a different scope, audience or subject.
claim: RFC 8693 defines a token-exchange grant type for changing token scope, audience, or subject in OAuth 2.0.

query: JWT Bearer Token delegation chains service-to-service authentication
title: AI agents and the multi-hop delegation problem — WorkOS
snippet: Token Exchange is used for service-to-service delegation in microservice architectures, where a backend service acts on behalf of the original user when calling downstream services. Auth0's On-Behalf-Of (OBO) token exchange implements the delegation pattern directly, where a middle-tier service exchanges the incoming user token for a new token scoped to the downstream API, preserving the user's identity while adding itself to the chain.
claim: Token exchange enables On-Behalf-Of delegation where middle-tier services exchange user tokens for downstream-scoped tokens.

topic: Delegation chain handling with act claims
query: JWT Bearer Token delegation chains service-to-service authentication
title: Delegation Done Right: Token Exchange and the On-Behalf-Of Pattern | CerberAuth
snippet: RFC 8693 supports representing delegation chains through nested "act" claims in JWT tokens, though prior-actor claims are informational only. When there is a chain of requests, each service in the middle of the chain must validate the incoming access token and then request a new access token where the scope, audience, client, issuer and role claims are such that the next service in the chain will accept it.
claim: RFC 8693 supports delegation chains through act claims in JWT tokens, with each service validating and re-scoping tokens.

query: SPIFFE SPIRE workload identity certificate authentication
title: What is SPIFFE? Universal Workload Identity Framework Guide - Palo Alto Networks
snippet: SPIFFE sets specifications for issuing and managing cryptographic identities for services across different environments. The core of this standard is the SPIFFE Verifiable Identity Document (SVID), a short-lived credential that serves as a workload's identity.
claim: SPIFFE defines workload identity using short-lived SPIFFE Verifiable Identity Documents (SVIDs) across environments.

query: SPIFFE SPIRE workload identity certificate authentication
title: SPIFFE Concepts | SPIFFE
snippet: X.509-SVID is an X.509 certificate in which the SPIFFE ID is embedded in the Subject Alternative Name (SAN) field as a URI, which integrates directly with mutual TLS (mTLS) — the standard mechanism for service-to-service authentication.
claim: X.509-SVID embeds SPIFFE IDs in certificate SAN fields for mutual TLS service-to-service authentication.

query: SPIFFE SPIRE workload identity certificate authentication
title: What are SPIFFE and SPIRE?
snippet: Every workload must undergo attestation—a process by which the SPIRE Agent verifies environmental attributes before issuing a SPIFFE ID, which ensures that identities are tied to real, verifiable conditions at runtime. SPIRE attests a workload against platform facts — which node, which ServiceAccount, which container — and issues a short-lived identity automatically, so there is no long-lived certificate to distribute or leak.
claim: SPIRE attests workloads against platform facts before issuing short-lived identities, eliminating long-lived certificate distribution.

topic: Trust bundle distribution and peer-to-peer verification
query: SPIFFE SPIRE workload identity certificate authentication
title: Working with SVIDs | SPIFFE
snippet: SPIRE distributes "trust bundles", collections of public keys, to all workloads, allowing them to verify the SVIDs presented by other services within the same or federated trust domains. Other workloads can then verify the SVID locally, enabling trusted, peer-to-peer authentication without the need to contact a central authority for every transaction.
claim: SPIRE distributes trust bundles enabling peer-to-peer SVID verification without central authority for each transaction.
